title: Internal: handling procedure for owed credits before a same-day maintenance fee waiver review
content:
## When this procedure applies

This runbook applies when the owner of an active Personal Checking account questions a monthly maintenance fee dated the current business day, the account's cycle closing date, while the account carries overdraft transfer fees charged contrary to the Personal Checking terms and a single submitted electronic-transaction dispute whose provisional credit has fallen due.

When the procedure is complete, the owed refunds and the owed provisional credit are on the ledger, the Relationship Balance waiver for the questioned fee has been judged on the resulting close-of-business Relationship Balance, and the fee has been refunded as a bank error when that waiver is met.

## Steps

| Step | Performed by | Action | Tool |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Agent | Refund an earlier overdraft transfer fee charged in error, under the general bank-error refund ground | refund_transfer_fee_error_033d9cbf |
| 2 | Agent | Refund the most recent overdraft transfer fee charged in error | refund_transfer_fee_error_033d9cbf |
| 3 | Agent | Post the provisional credit that has fallen due on the submitted dispute | post_dispute_provisional_credit_5453b90d |
| 4 | Agent | Judge the Relationship Balance waiver and refund the questioned maintenance fee | refund_same_day_maintenance_fee_e9518b99 |

Every step is performed by the agent; the procedure has no step performed by the customer themselves.

## Why the steps run in this order

- **Step 1 before step 2, and step 2 before step 3.** The same-day waiver review posts the fee refunds in the order the fees posted, and all of them before the dispute credit. So the earlier transfer fee is refunded first, the most recent one next, and the provisional credit after both.
- **Step 3 before step 4.** The same rule posts every owed credit before the Relationship Balance waiver is judged, because pending credits that have not posted do not count. Judging the waiver first would measure a Relationship Balance without the owed credits.

## What passes from step to step

```
Step 1 refund  ─┐
Step 2 refund  ─┼─> each posting raises the account's ledger balance
Step 3 credit  ─┘            │
                             v
Step 4: the Relationship Balance waiver is judged on that raised ledger balance
```

What step 4 uses from steps 1 to 3 is the account's ledger balance, which each posting raises on the account itself rather than as a figure carried in the entry it writes; no step hands a value to the next in any other way.

## Ordering Q&A

**Q: Is there any waiting between steps?**
A: No step depends on a real-world event or the passage of time; each is a posting the agent completes in the same contact.

**Q: Does the owner have to consent to or claim any of these postings?**
A: No. None of the postings is an owner's consent or claim under the Personal Checking terms, which is why no step is the customer's.

**Counter-example: steps 3 and 4 swapped.** If the waiver were judged before the provisional credit posted, the Relationship Balance would be measured without that owed credit, which the ordering rule forbids.

**Counter-example: steps 1 and 2 swapped.** The most recent transfer fee would be refunded before the earlier one, which breaks the rule that fee refunds post in the order the fees posted.
